title: The Gift of the Magi
summary: A poor young couple each sacrifice their most valuable possession to buy the other a Christmas present.

source.author: O. Henry
source.note: Retold from the plot in new C1 English by Lexkite; no sentences copied from the original text.

license: Adaptation CC BY 4.0 Lexkite; original story in the public domain

cover.scene: Flat 2D illustration: a small bare apartment at Christmas with a pocket watch chain and a set of hair combs on a table, snow at the window, no text

chapters.title: Della's Sacrifice
sentences: On the day before Christmas, Della counted her money for the third time and found only a tiny amount.
She had saved every coin for months by being frugal, yet it was not nearly enough for a decent gift.
Her husband, Jim, owned only two treasures: a gold watch from his father and a modest salary.
Della owned one treasure as well, a cascade of long brown hair that reached below her knees.
She stood in front of the window for a long while, and a single tear fell onto the worn carpet.
Then she put on her old jacket, brushed her hair one last time, and hurried out into the cold street.
At a small shop, a woman who bought hair for hats offered her twenty dollars without a moment of hesitation.
Della accepted the offer, and the sacrifice felt strangely light because she was thinking only of Jim.
Two hours later she found the perfect present, a plain platinum chain for his beloved watch.
She paid twenty-one dollars for it and hurried home with the remaining eighty-seven cents.
In the mirror, her short curls made her look like a schoolboy, and she felt suddenly anxious.
She prayed quietly that Jim would still find her pretty when he walked through the door.

quiz.explain: A woman who bought hair for hats paid her twenty dollars.

quiz.explain: She bought a plain platinum chain for his beloved watch.

quiz.q: How did Della feel at the end of the chapter?

chapters.title: Jim's Reaction
sentences: When Jim came home, he stopped in the doorway and stared at Della with an expression she could not read.
It was not anger, nor surprise, nor disapproval, but a strange look that frightened her more than any of those.
Della explained that she had cut and sold her hair, and that it would grow back soon enough.
Jim hugged her tightly and said that no haircut could ever make him love her less.
Then he placed a small package on the table and asked her to open it before saying anything else.
Inside lay a set of beautiful combs, the very ones she had admired in a shop window for a year.
They were expensive and now completely useless, because the hair they were designed for no longer existed.
Della laughed through her tears and held the combs against her chest like precious jewels.
Then she remembered her own gift and offered him the chain with a trembling, eager smile.
Jim sat down slowly and confessed that he had sold his watch to pay for the combs.
They both realised how silly and how generous they had been, and neither of them felt any regret.
The narrator says that such givers are the wisest of all, because love was the only treasure they truly needed.

quiz.explain: He gave her a set of beautiful combs.

options: She had no long hair to use them.
quiz.explain: Her hair had been cut and sold.

quiz.q: What had Jim done to pay for the combs?
quiz.explain: He confessed that he had sold his watch.
